title: Kieron Pollard Reclaims All-Time T20 Run Record With Blistering CPL Knock
excerpt: The 39-year-old Trinidadian smashed 65 off 26 balls to overtake Jos Buttler and reclaim the top spot on T20 cricket's all-time run charts with 14,921 career runs.
body:
• Kieron Pollard reclaimed the all-time T20 run-scoring record with 14,921 career runs, surpassing Jos Buttler's 14,890, during a CPL 2026 match for Trinbago Knight Riders against St Lucia Kings.
  • Pollard smashed 65 off just 26 balls at a strike rate of 250, hitting six fours and five sixes, though TKR lost the match by 36 runs.
  • The record has changed hands three times in 2026 — Pollard broke Chris Gayle's 12-year reign in June, Buttler surpassed him in August during The Hundred, and Pollard has now reclaimed it.
  • Pollard's five sixes took his career tally to 1,010 maximums, putting him 47 away from matching Gayle's all-time record of 1,057 T20 sixes.

Kieron Pollard has reclaimed his place at the summit of T20 cricket's all-time run charts. The 39-year-old Trinidadian blasted 65 off 26 balls for Trinbago Knight Riders against St Lucia Kings in the Caribbean Premier League on Tuesday, taking his career tally to 14,921 runs and overtaking England's Jos Buttler, who sits on 14,890.

It was the third time the record has changed hands in 2026 alone — a year that has turned T20 cricket's most prestigious batting milestone into a three-way tug of war.

A Record That Won't Stay Still

The all-time T20 run-scoring record had belonged to Chris Gayle for over 12 years, dating back to March 2014. Pollard finally toppled the Jamaican's long-standing mark of 14,562 runs in June, scoring an unbeaten century for MI New York against Washington Freedom in Major League Cricket.

But the record barely had time to settle. In August, Jos Buttler surpassed Pollard's tally during a blistering knock in The Hundred for Manchester Super Giants against Welsh Fire, taking the lead with 14,890 runs.

Pollard needed 35 runs heading into the CPL match to reclaim the top spot. He went well beyond that. Batting at No. 6, he struck six fours and five sixes during a 26-ball stay that produced runs at a strike rate of 250. His five sixes also pushed his career tally to 1,010 maximums — 47 short of Gayle's all-time T20 record of 1,057.

"We know how difficult this game is, and at the moment it's all about guiding them and being there for them and trying to teach them and help them when they make mistakes."

— Nicholas Pooran, TKR captain

Match Goes to the Kings Despite Pollard's Fireworks

Pollard's heroics came in a losing cause. St Lucia Kings posted a mammoth 211/4 in 20 overs, built on an unbeaten century from New Zealand wicketkeeper-batter Tim Seifert, who smashed 105 off 61 balls with eight fours and five sixes. Charith Asalanka contributed 33 off 21 deliveries, and John Campbell added a brisk 27 off 17.

TKR's chase started well, with Sunil Narine making 25 off 14 and Colin Munro scoring 48 off 35. But Roston Chase ripped the heart out of the middle order, taking three wickets in five deliveries — removing Narine, Leus du Plooy Breetzke, and Nicholas Pooran in quick succession.

Pollard's explosive counter-attack kept TKR in the contest, but Matthew Forde ended his innings with a return catch. TKR were eventually restricted to 175/6, falling 36 runs short. The result moved St Lucia Kings to the top of the CPL points table.

The T20 Run-Scoring Leaderboard

The all-time top five now reads: Pollard (14,921 runs in 749 matches), Buttler (14,890 in 526), Gayle (14,562 in 463), Alex Hales (14,489 in 531), and David Warner (14,284 in 439). Pollard's numbers are a testament to longevity — he has played more T20 matches than anyone in history, and his 749 appearances span nearly two decades of franchise cricket across the globe.

Pollard will have a chance to extend his lead and potentially become the first batter to reach 15,000 T20 runs when TKR face Barbados Tridents in their next CPL fixture.

A Name That Resonates Across India

For Indian cricket fans, Pollard remains one of the most beloved overseas players in IPL history. His decade-long association with Mumbai Indians, where he played alongside Rohit Sharma and Jasprit Bumrah and won multiple titles, made him a household name across the country. His power-hitting exploits in the MI blue and gold defined an era of IPL cricket, and his continued dominance at 39 only adds to the legend.

The record may yet change hands again — Buttler continues to pile on runs in The Hundred and is only 31 runs behind. But for now, the crown sits where many T20 fans believe it belongs: with the most prolific appearance-maker the format has ever seen.
